hook.text: Inuit traditionally eat almost no plants—mostly seal, whale, and fish. Yet they don't get scurvy.

buildup.text: Raw and fermented marine foods retain vitamin C that cooking destroys. Preparation methods matter.

discovery.text: Inuit also carry genetic variants that help metabolize high-fat diets efficiently.

twist.text: When Western diets replaced traditional foods, diabetes and heart disease rates skyrocketed in Arctic peoples.

climax.text: Their genes adapted to one diet over millennia. Switch the diet, and the adaptation becomes a liability.

punchline.text: Their genes fit their food—not ours.

quiz.question: How did Inuit avoid nutrient deficiencies on a mostly meat diet?
options: Raw and fermented marine foods retained key vitamins
